_doc: Google Store Trade-In max published values per model id (Google's values are promotional credits toward a new Pixel). Refreshed weekly by scripts/refresh-google-comps.py via .github/workflows/refresh-comps.yml (its old URL now 404s, see _verification). Frontend reads this at runtime when device is in the Google family (pixel / pixelwatch / google_tab). CONVENTION: only include a value Google actually lists. notAccepted = model ids a manual check confirmed Google does NOT take; only those get the 'Google won't take this on trade-in' claim. A model with no value and not in notAccepted makes no claim either way.

_verification.2026-09-16: Manual check (Powerhouse). The Google Store publishes no value table (the estimate lives inside checkout), so values come from the post-launch Pixel 11 Pro (256 GB) trade-in list reported by 9to5google on 2026-08-28: Pixel 10 Pro Fold $850, 10 Pro XL $650, 10 Pro $550, 10 $460, 9 Pro Fold $630, 9 Pro XL $500, 9 Pro $480, 9 $350, 8 Pro $420, 8 $350, 8a $180, Fold $450, 7 Pro $340, 7 $280, 6 Pro $300, 6 $230, 6a $100, 5 $150. Google accepts the Pixel 10 family (9to5google 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-28).
_verification.removed: px9a (was 135), px7a (was 10) and px5a (was 30) are in neither Google list (9to5google 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-28), and Google pays $100 for the older 4a and 6a and $180 for the 8a, so those snapshot values look wrong, not just stale. Removed from values and from GOOGLE_MODEL_LABELS; with no value the /sell pages make no claim. For scale, Samsung's own table (tradeInJson, 2026-09-16) credits $150 / $103 / $45 for them.
_verification.unverified: pw3, pw2, pw1 and gpixeltab are not in Google's list either; their values are still the 2026-05-24 snapshot (no /sell page uses them; the homepage comparison panel does).
